meta.expect: 'put it in an email', no list

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste either of our time. Before you say a word about Owen's essay, tell me who decided on that zero, and why I found out about it after my son saw it on his phone in the middle of class.
I didn't come for thanks, Hale. Who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

Turn the screen, I want to read it myself. I'm writing down "11:31 PM" and "two pastes six minutes apart." A paste tells you when words arrived in that file, Hale, not who wrote them or where, and you still haven't told me whether anyone asked Owen before that zero went in.
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. Nothing is agreed: the zero comes off, and I'm still waiting to hear whether Owen was asked a single question before it went in.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.
I'm not taking dictation for you, Hale. Did you speak to Owen before November 3, yes or no?
